findings.source_passage: strange subterranean commotions in him, which seemed to have egress at his other buried extremity, causing the waters behind him to upbubble
findings.source_locator: description of the old bull whale, after 'coming forth with a choking sort of gush, and spending itself in torn shreds'
findings.why_it_matters: This grotesque scatological detail is textually distinctive and characteristic of Melville's comic-naturalist register; the draft omits it entirely, flattening the old bull's comic-pathetic portrait to mere jaundice and a stump.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore 'spending itself in torn shreds, followed by strange subterranean commotions in him, which seemed to have egress at his other buried extremity, causing the waters behind him to upbubble' in the whale description paragraph.

findings.source_passage: We all know what an astonishing atmospheric weight we ourselves stand up under… how vast, then, the burden of a whale, bearing on his back a column of two hundred fathoms of ocean! It must at least equal the weight of fifty atmospheres. One whaleman has estimated it at the weight of twenty line-of-battle ships
findings.source_locator: expository digression after 'the longer the stricken whale stays under water, the more he is exhausted'
findings.why_it_matters: This is Melville's signature cetological-expository voice at full stretch — precise figures, analogical piling, rhetorical escalation — entirely replaced in the draft by a single subordinate clause ('the vast pressure of the sea'), erasing a sustained paragraph of narrator consciousness.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the atmospheric-weight digression, including the fifty-atmospheres figure and the twenty-line-of-battle-ships estimate, even in lightly compressed form.

findings.source_passage: young whales, in the highest health, and swelling with noble aspirations, prematurely cut off in the warm flush and May of life, with all their panting lard about them; even these brawny, buoyant heroes do sometimes sink
findings.source_locator: buoyancy digression, after 'it is not so. For young whales…'
findings.why_it_matters: This ironic elegy for young whales — 'noble aspirations,' 'warm flush and May of life,' 'panting lard' — is one of the segment's most distinctive passages of Melvillean mock-heroic pathos; its entire voice texture is absent in the draft.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore at least the core ironic formulation: 'young whales, in the highest health, and swelling with noble aspirations, prematurely cut off in the warm flush and May of life' before the compressed summary.

findings.source_passage: the fear of this vast dumb brute of the sea, was chained up and enchanted in him
findings.why_it_matters: 'Chained up and enchanted' is a rhetorically precise doublet; the draft reduces it to 'chained in him,' dropping the 'enchanted' which carries the thematic weight of the whale's inwardness.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore 'chained up and enchanted in him' verbatim.

findings.source_passage: It might have been darted by some Nor' West Indian long before America was discovered.
findings.source_locator: stone lance-head passage, after 'a lance-head of stone being found in him'
findings.why_it_matters: This speculative sentence opens the whale's body onto deep historical time and is a small but characteristic moment of Melvillean interpretive reach; the draft notes the stone lance but drops the historical speculation.
findings.suggested_fix: Add the sentence 'It might have been darted by some Nor' West Indian long before America was discovered' after the stone lance-head is mentioned.

summary: The draft faithfully preserves most dialogue and set-pieces but erases three sustained voice passages — the scatological upbubble detail on the old bull, the atmospheric-pressure digression with its precise figures, and the mock-heroic elegy for young whales — constituting three medium-severity findings that trigger regeneration.
